raw_response:
I am 65 years old and have farmed these 5 mu in Quzhou County for 40 years. My household is just my wife and me now, so I need a plan we can manage with our own labor. I grow only cotton — this land suits it, and after four decades I know every pest and weather pattern. At the start of the season in mid‑April, I will rotary‑till the field and sow improved cotton seed, the kind we call guoxinmian or similar new lines from the seed shop; the old traditional seeds are long gone because these improved ones resist bollworm and give steadier yields. For fertilizer, I will spread about 100 kg of compound fertilizer per mu as a basal dressing — something like 15‑15‑15 or 20‑10‑21 — and add a little urea at flowering time. That works out to roughly 25 kg of nitrogen, 15 kg of phosphorus, and 15 kg of potassium per mu, which is enough for cotton without wasting money. Because I have a well, I will irrigate three times: right after sowing, at flowering, and during boll filling. Cotton pests never rest in this county, so I will spray insecticides about twelve times through the season, watching mainly for aphids, spider mites, and the occasional bollworm escape. If the weather is normal, I expect to pick around 550 kg of seed cotton per mu come October.
